name: Cooke College Scholarship Program
who: High school seniors with strong grades and financial need who plan to attend a four-year college. Last-dollar award: it fills the gap left after the college's own aid. Past winners averaged a 3.99 unweighted GPA.
notes: Applied for through the Common App. One of the largest private scholarships in the country.

name: Daniels Scholarship Program
amount: Up to full cost at partner schools; up to $25,000 a year elsewhere
who: Residents of Colorado, New Mexico, Utah or Wyoming with an unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher and household adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less. U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
notes: Closes at 4:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Up to $7,500 a year at non-partner schools inside the four-state region.

name: Voice of Democracy
awards: Awards at post, district, state and national level
who: Students in grades 9-12. Record a short audio essay on this year's theme, "What a Veteran Taught Me About America," and hand it with the entry form to a participating local VFW post.
notes: Entries go to your local VFW post by midnight, October 31. Smaller prizes at the local and state rounds make this worth entering even if you don't expect to win nationally.

name: Regeneron Science Talent Search
awards: 40 finalists share more than $1.8 million; about $3.1 million awarded in all
who: High school seniors who have completed an original, independent research project and can submit a full research report and application.
notes: Closes at 8 p.m. Eastern. Only realistic if you already have a research project; read the official rules for exact eligibility.

name: Elks Most Valuable Student
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors planning a four-year degree. No Elks connection needed. Judged on scholarship, leadership and financial need.
notes: The Elks site was down when checked; the date comes from two scholarship directories. Confirm it before relying on it.

name: National Honor Society Scholarship
who: High school seniors who are active members in good standing of a National Honor Society chapter, with an NHS student account verified by the chapter adviser.
notes: Closes at 5 p.m. Eastern. Ask your adviser to verify your account early; that step is what holds people up.

name: Ron Brown Scholarship
who: Black or African American high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, with a strong academic record, leadership, community service and financial need.
notes: Counselor recommendation and transcript are due December 15. Online only; late applications are not accepted.

name: SMART Scholarship-for-Service
amount: Full tuition plus a $30,000 to $46,000 yearly stipend
who: Students in an approved technical field (computer science, engineering, math, physical sciences and similar), at least 18, with a 3.0 GPA, able to hold a security clearance. Incoming college freshmen have been eligible since 2023.
notes: You owe one year of civilian work at a Defense Department lab for each year funded, and it includes summer internships. Deadline is the first Friday of December; directories disagree by a day or two, so check the portal.

name: Science Ambassador Scholarship
who: Women and non-binary high school seniors or undergraduates in a STEM major attending college in the U.S. Citizenship is not required.
notes: The application is a public YouTube video, three minutes or less, teaching any STEM topic. No essay, no transcript.

name: Burger King Scholars
who: High school seniors in the U.S., Puerto Rico or Canada planning two- or four-year college or vocational school. Considers GPA, work experience, activities, community service and need.
notes: Closes early once 30,000 applications arrive, so apply the week it opens. Most awards are $1,000, and thousands are given. Dates and the 2.5 GPA come from directories, not the sponsor's page.

name: Equitable Excellence Scholarship
who: High school seniors in the 50 states, D.C. or Puerto Rico with a 2.5 GPA or higher who show drive and a record of giving back to their community.
notes: Date is from scholarship directories and matches last year's (December 18, 2025). Run by Scholarship America.

name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors with a 3.0 GPA or higher, planning full-time study at a four-year college. Looks for leadership, drive, integrity and citizenship.
notes: Date is last cycle's (January 5, 2026, noon Central) moved forward a year; the new cycle wasn't posted when checked.

name: Live Más Scholarship
awards: Up to $14.5 million in total last cycle
who: Ages 16 to 26, legal U.S. residents, heading to or enrolled in a two-year, four-year, vocational or trade program. No GPA or test score requirements; it's about your passion and the impact you want to make.
notes: The sponsor says 2027 applications open this fall; the date shown is last cycle's (October 14, 2025 to January 6, 2026) moved forward.

name: Dell Scholars
amount: $20,000 plus a laptop and book credits
who: Seniors graduating from a Texas high school who took part in an approved college readiness program in grades 11 and 12, are Pell Grant eligible, have at least a 2.4 GPA and plan to attend a four-year public college in Texas.
notes: This used to be a national program; it is now limited to Texas students attending Texas public universities.

name: Jackie Robinson Foundation Scholarship
who: U.S. citizens graduating from high school with financial need, academic excellence, leadership potential and a dedication to community service, planning to attend an approved four-year college.
notes: Closes at 5:00 p.m. Eastern. Past cycles also required the CSS Profile and a recommendation letter by the same date.

name: APIA Scholarship
who: Undergraduates with high financial need who are U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents (or citizens of the Marshall Islands, Micronesia or Palau), enrolled or enrolling in a U.S. accredited college.
notes: APIA Scholars serves Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander students. The page checked did not spell out a heritage requirement, so read the eligibility section before applying.

name: Army ROTC High School Scholarship
amount: Full tuition and fees (or room and board), $420 a month, $1,200 a year for books
who: U.S. citizens aged 17 to under 31 at commissioning, with an unweighted high school GPA of at least 2.50 and an SAT or ACT score on file.
notes: Three selection rounds: October 12, 2026 (passed), January 18, 2027 and March 8, 2027. Earlier rounds have more money. Comes with an eight-year service commitment (active duty, Reserve or National Guard).

name: HSF Scholar Program
who: Students of Hispanic heritage who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or DACA recipients, planning full-time study at a four-year college. Minimum 3.0 GPA for high school students (2.5 for college students). FAFSA required.
notes: Date is last cycle's (January 5 to February 15, 2026) moved forward a year. Being named an HSF Scholar also opens mentoring and career programs, even without a cash award.

name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
amount: Up to $33,000 for tuition plus $6,000 for books and travel
who: Undocumented students (with or without DACA or TPS) who came to the U.S. before November 1, 2020 and before age 16, with a 2.5 GPA, significant unmet need and no Pell Grant eligibility.
notes: The sponsor confirms the next round opens November 1, 2026; the closing date shown is last round's (February 28, 2026) moved forward. For use at partner colleges.

name: SWE Scholarships
who: Students who identify as women studying engineering, engineering technology or computer science. Incoming first-year students, including high school seniors, use the Emerging First Year application.
notes: One application is matched against every SWE scholarship you qualify for. Current college students apply earlier: December 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027.

name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
who: Young people aged 8 to 18 living in the U.S. or Canada who have led a significant service project helping people or the environment.
notes: Two steps last cycle: a pre-application by March 15 and the full application by April 15. Dates shown are 2026's moved forward a year.

name: American Indian College Fund Scholarships
awards: Thousands each year, from one application
who: Native American and Alaska Native students (enrolled tribal members or descendants) attending a tribal college or other accredited college.
notes: The application opens February 1 every year, and May 31 is the priority date. One application covers all of the Fund's scholarships.

name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
who: Students 18 or younger, U.S. citizens or permanent residents, who have completed a significant piece of work in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, literature, music, philosophy or "outside the box."
notes: The 2027 application opens this fall; the closing date wasn't posted when checked (past cycles closed in mid-February). The music category takes a performance or composition portfolio.

name: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
amount: Up to $10,000 a year plus a paid Amazon internship
who: High school seniors planning a bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, with financial need and a 2.3 GPA or higher, who have taken a computer science course (or take Amazon's assessment). U.S. citizen, permanent resident or authorized to work.
notes: The new cycle's dates weren't posted when checked; past cycles closed in mid-winter. Check back in November.

name: Evans Scholarship
who: Golf caddies with a strong caddie record, excellent grades, demonstrated financial need and outstanding character.
notes: Only for students who have worked as caddies. The site didn't list this year's closing date when checked; past deadlines fell in late October, so look now.

name: Hagan Scholarship
amount: Up to $7,500 a semester for 8 semesters, plus $1,000 for college supplies
who: High school seniors with a 3.50 GPA or higher, household income under the foundation's limit, and at least 240 hours of paid work in the past year. Historically aimed at students from rural counties.
notes: The site's pages gave two different income limits ($100,000 and $125,000) and no closing date when checked. Read the eligibility page; past cycles closed around December 1.

name: Air Force ROTC High School Scholarship
sponsor: U.S. Air Force and Space Force
amount: Tuition scholarships of several types, plus a monthly stipend
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors willing to serve as Air Force or Space Force officers after graduating. Technical majors are favored.
notes: The official page blocked automated checking, so no dates are listed here. Past application windows closed around the turn of the year; look it up now if you're interested.

name: Navy ROTC National Scholarship
amount: Full tuition and fees, book stipend, monthly allowance
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors willing to serve as Navy or Marine Corps officers after graduating.
notes: The official page blocked automated checking, so no dates are listed here. Past deadlines fell at the end of January.

name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
amount: More than $203,500 in scholarships nationally in 2026
awards: Awards at post, state and national level
who: High school students who prepare and deliver a speech about the U.S. Constitution, starting at a local American Legion post.
notes: State winners were named in April and the national final was in May last year. Contact your local post or state Legion office now; local dates vary.

name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
amount: Varies; national scholarships for top senior portfolios
who: Teen artists and writers. Seniors can submit a portfolio, which is what the largest scholarships are tied to.
notes: Deadlines are set by region and start in December; find yours on the site. Entry costs $15 per work or $40 per portfolio, and the fee is waived for anyone who says they can't afford it.

name: UNCF Scholarships
awards: Dozens of programs through one portal
who: Each program sets its own rules. Many support Black students and students at historically Black colleges, and several are for STEM majors.
notes: Create one profile at opportunities.uncf.org and it shows the programs you qualify for. Several close in October, so check now.

name: Ayn Rand Essay Contests
who: Students write an essay on Anthem or The Fountainhead (ages 13 and up) or Atlas Shrugged (high school, college and graduate students). International students may enter.
notes: The next deadline was listed as "TBD" when checked.

name: Profile in Courage Essay Contest
who: U.S. high school students in grades 9-12, writing about an act of political courage by an elected official.
notes: The official page blocked automated checking. Past contests closed in mid-January; confirm the prize and date on the site.

name: Stamps Scholarship
amount: Up to full cost of attendance, plus funds for study abroad and research
who: Top applicants to the program's partner universities. You don't apply to Stamps directly; each partner picks its own scholars from its applicant pool.
notes: Check each partner university's own page: many require applying by an early scholarship deadline (often November 1 or December 1).

name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program
who: High school seniors with a 3.0 GPA or higher who are U.S. citizens, nationals, permanent residents or otherwise eligible for federal aid. Based on leadership, academics and service, not financial need.
notes: First round needs no essays, transcript or recommendations. About 1% of applicants advance to semifinalist.

name: The Gates Scholarship
amount: Full cost of attendance not covered by other aid
who: Pell-eligible high school seniors with a weighted GPA of 3.3 or higher who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, planning a four-year degree at a nonprofit college.
notes: Opens in mid-July, before senior year starts, which is why many students miss it.

name: QuestBridge National College Match
who: High-achieving high school seniors from low-income families, typically household income under $65,000 a year for a family of four with minimal assets.
notes: Matches cover tuition, housing and food with no loans and no parent contribution. Juniors should look at QuestBridge's College Prep Scholars program in the spring.

name: YoungArts National Arts Competition
who: Artists aged 15-18 or in grades 10-12 in classical music, jazz, voice, dance, design, film, photography, theater, visual arts or writing. U.S. citizens, permanent residents or others able to receive U.S. income.
notes: This year's competition has closed; the next application opens in summer 2027. Winners become eligible for nomination as U.S. Presidential Scholars in the Arts.

name: Cameron Impact Scholarship
amount: Full tuition, fees and books for four years
who: U.S. citizens with an unweighted GPA of 3.7 or higher, strong leadership and community service. The application is now filled in during junior year.
notes: The class of 2027 round closed May 1, 2026 (or earlier, once 3,000 eligible applications arrived). The foundation's site blocked automated checking; details are from a high school counseling page.

name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
who: High school juniors who are U.S. citizens with a 2.0 GPA or higher and family adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less, who have overcome significant adversity.
notes: The site lists this award for juniors and didn't show dates when checked. It also lists scholarships for seniors tied to specific states and universities (Montana, Arizona State, Long Island University and others).

name: Coolidge Scholarship
amount: Full ride: tuition, room, board and expenses for four years
who: High school juniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Need-blind; academic excellence is the main criterion.
notes: For students starting college in fall 2028. Essays draw on The Autobiography of Calvin Coolidge, so allow several weeks. Date is from scholarship directories.

name: National Merit Scholarship Program
awards: About 16,000 semifinalists; roughly half of finalists win
who: You enter by taking the PSAT/NMSQT in October of junior year. Semifinalists are named the following September by state cutoff score.
notes: Seniors: if you were named a Semifinalist in September 2026, the finalist application was due October 7 and confirming SAT or ACT scores must reach NMSC by December 31, 2026. Many colleges give their own large awards to finalists, often worth far more than the national one.

name: Posse Scholarship
amount: Full tuition at a partner college
who: Students with leadership and academic potential, nominated by their high school or a community organization. Not based on need or background.
opens: Nominations open in spring of junior year
notes: You can't apply on your own: ask your counselor to nominate you in the spring or summer before senior year. Deadlines vary by city.

name: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars
who: Students chosen for academic success, community service and financial need who are leaders in their communities. You do not need to work at Chick-fil-A.
notes: Separate from the smaller scholarships Chick-fil-A gives its own restaurant team members.

name: Award for Aspirations in Computing
sponsor: National Center for Women & Information Technology (NCWIT)
amount: Prizes, plus scholarships open only to award recipients
who: High school students in grades 9-12 who are women, genderqueer or non-binary and are active in computing, attending school in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands or a U.S. military base overseas.
notes: Closes at 10:00 p.m. Eastern. The prize list on the site is an image and could not be read, so check it there. Recipients join a community that many college scholarships recruit from.

name: Hispanic Heritage Youth Awards
amount: Gold, silver and bronze grants (amounts not posted)
who: High school seniors graduating in spring 2027 with an unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher. Categories: community service, engineering, green, technology, and journalism and media.
notes: The page showed two different dates (November 1, 2026 and November 2, 2025), so confirm. It did not spell out a heritage requirement; the program honors Latino students.

name: Work Ethic Scholarship
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors or graduates enrolling in a trade program of two years or less: construction, welding, HVAC, transportation, technology and others. Four-year degrees do not qualify.
notes: Needs a signed S.W.E.A.T. Pledge with four short answers, a video, two references, a transcript and a tuition bill. The page gave October 31 without a year.

name: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program
amount: Full four-year scholarship at Duke or UNC-Chapel Hill
who: High school seniors applying to Duke University or the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. It has its own application, separate from the universities'.
notes: The early window closed October 15, 2026; November 15 is the date for everyone else. The page checked did not list what the award covers; it has historically paid tuition, housing, food and summer programs.

name: Greenhouse Scholars
amount: Up to $5,000 a year, with mentoring and internship support
who: Graduating high school seniors with an unweighted GPA of 3.5 or higher and household income no greater than $80,000, living in Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, New York, North Carolina, Utah or parts of California.
notes: In California only Los Angeles, Riverside and Orange counties qualify.

name: Cooke Undergraduate Transfer Scholarship
amount: Up to $55,000 a year for two to three years
who: Top community college students with financial need who plan to transfer to a four-year college to finish a bachelor's degree.
notes: Last-dollar award, applied after the college's own aid. Only for students currently at a community college.

name: NESA Eagle Scout Scholarships
awards: Several award levels from one application
who: Eagle Scouts who are NESA members and are enrolled full time in a degree or skilled-trade program, from senior year of high school through junior year of college.
notes: Closes at 11:59 p.m. Central. The top awards are four-year scholarships of $50,000 and $30,000.

name: ScholarSHPE
who: Active SHPE members with a 2.5 GPA or higher who are pursuing a STEM degree. High school seniors can apply.
notes: Date is last cycle's (February 2 to 16, 2026) moved forward a year. The window is only two weeks long, so join SHPE and prepare beforehand.

name: Engebretson Foundation Scholarship
who: High school seniors recognized for academic achievement and leadership.
notes: You can reapply each year of college. Past cycles also asked for financial need and strong test scores; read the requirements when it opens.

name: Create-A-Greeting-Card Scholarship Contest
amount: Cash scholarship for the winning design
who: Students aged 14 or older enrolled in high school, college or homeschool. Submit one original artwork or photo for the front of a greeting card.
notes: The page checked did not show the prize amount; past contests paid $10,000 to the winner. No essay, just the artwork.

name: AISES Scholarships
sponsor: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
who: Indigenous students (tribal citizens or descendants, Native Hawaiians, Pacific Islanders, Canadian Indigenous) who are AISES members studying STEM full time. Minimum GPA runs from 2.0 to 3.0 depending on the award.
notes: Opens December 15 and closes April 30 each year. One award for trade students adds money for tools.

name: Edison Scholars
who: High school seniors living in Southern California Edison's service area, with a 3.0 GPA or higher and financial need, who plan to study an eligible STEM major at a four-year college.
notes: Only for parts of Southern California served by Southern California Edison. The site says the 2027 application opens this fall but gave no dates yet.

name: Stokes Educational Scholarship Program
amount: Up to $30,000 a year for tuition, plus a year-round salary
who: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors, able to get a security clearance, with at least a 1200 SAT or 25 ACT and a 3.0 GPA. Majors include computer science, cybersecurity, AI, data science, mathematics, and computer or electrical engineering.
notes: You work summers at NSA and owe one and a half times your years of study afterward. Past deadlines ranged from October 31 to November 30 and this year's could not be confirmed, so check immediately.

name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
awards: Up to 30 a year in three tiers
who: High school seniors of Hispanic heritage who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or DACA recipients. Need-based, with merit considered.
notes: The official page blocked automated checking and directories disagree on the details: deadlines range from February 5 to February 24, and the minimum GPA from 2.5 to 3.0. Confirm on the site.

name: Morehead-Cain Scholarship
amount: Full four-year scholarship at UNC-Chapel Hill
who: High school seniors nominated by their school or an affiliated program. North Carolina residents and students at North Carolina high schools may nominate themselves.
notes: Ask your counselor now whether your school nominates. The portal did not list this year's dates when checked; past deadlines fell in October.

name: Jefferson Scholarship
amount: Full cost of attendance at UVA for four years
who: High school seniors nominated by their school. Each eligible school may put forward a student, who then goes through regional and final selection.
notes: You cannot apply on your own: ask your counselor whether your school is a nominating school and when it chooses. Worth over $83,000 a year for students from outside Virginia.

name: Optimist Oratorical Contest
amount: $2,500 at district level, up to $15,000 at the world championship
awards: Awards at district, regional and world level
who: Students under 19 on October 1 who have not finished high school. Give a short speech on this year's topic, "How My Actions Strengthen Those Around Me," through a local Optimist Club.
notes: Each club sets its own date; most finish by late March. Email programs@optimist.org to find a club near you.

name: John Lennon Award
who: Songwriters and composers of contemporary music aged 17 to 24, living in the U.S. Submit one original song as an audio file with a lyric sheet.
notes: The page did not list this cycle's dates; the last age cutoff was February 15, which suggests a mid-February deadline. The BMI Foundation runs other composer awards from the same site.

name: Poetry Out Loud
sponsor: National Endowment for the Arts and Poetry Foundation
amount: Cash awards at state and national finals
who: Students in grades 9-12. You memorize and recite poems, starting with a contest at your school, then state and national finals.
opens: School contests run in fall and winter
notes: Your school has to be registered with your state's Poetry Out Loud coordinator; homeschooled students contact the coordinator directly. The page checked did not list prize amounts; past national champions received $20,000.

name: Samsung American Legion Scholarship
who: Students who attend American Legion Boys State or Auxiliary Girls State in the summer after junior year and are direct descendants of a wartime U.S. veteran.
notes: Due by the end of the first day of your state's Boys State or Girls State session, so apply before you go.

name: Scholarships for Military Children
awards: At least one at every commissary that gets qualifying applications
who: Children of active duty, reserve and retired military members.
notes: The page did not list this cycle's dates when checked; past applications ran from mid-December to mid-February.

name: National High School Essay Contest
amount: $2,500, a trip to Washington and a Semester at Sea voyage
who: Students in grades 9-12 in the U.S. or U.S. citizens abroad, writing 1,000 to 1,500 words on a diplomacy topic. Children of Foreign Service members are excluded.
notes: The last contest has closed and the next one was not posted when checked; past deadlines fell in early April.

name: BigFuture Scholarships
who: Students in the classes of 2027 and 2028. No essay, GPA or test score: you earn entries by completing college-planning steps on your BigFuture dashboard, such as building a college list and filing the FAFSA.
notes: A drawing, not a competition, so the odds are long, but the steps are ones you need to do anyway. Finishing each step earlier gives more chances.

name: Point Foundation Scholarships
amount: Varies, with mentoring and leadership training
awards: Flagship, Access and Career & Technical awards
who: LGBTQ+ and ally students at accredited U.S. colleges. The Access scholarship is for low-income or first-generation students; a separate award covers trade and vocational programs.
notes: Three of the applications were open when checked, but the page did not list closing dates. Look now.

name: United States Senate Youth Program
sponsor: The Hearst Foundations and the U.S. Senate
who: High school juniors and seniors who hold an elected or appointed leadership post for the whole school year, such as student body or class officer, student council representative, or National Honor Society officer. U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Selected by each state's education department.
notes: December 1, 2026 is the national date by which states must name their delegates; each state sets an earlier student deadline, listed on the program's State Contacts and Deadlines page. Winners also spend Washington Week (March 6-13, 2027) in D.C. with all costs paid.

name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
who: High school students who make a short original video explaining a big idea or concept in physics, life sciences or mathematics.
notes: The winner's teacher also gets $50,000 and the school a $100,000 science lab. The 2026 challenge closed September 15, 2026; watch for the next one.

name: National Washington Crossing Foundation Scholarship
who: High school seniors who are U.S. citizens and plan a career in local, state or federal government service. One-page essay (300 words or fewer) on why you want a government career and what inspires you about George Washington's crossing of the Delaware.
notes: Sent by mail: three copies of the essay and of a recommendation from your principal or counselor, plus transcript and test scores, postmarked by January 15, 2027.

name: Glenn Miller Scholarship Competition
who: High school seniors and college freshmen who plan to make music their focus, in a vocal or an instrumental category. Finalists perform in person in Clarinda, Iowa, at their own travel cost.
notes: The date shown is the 2026 deadline; the 2027 date has not been posted yet. Prizes in each category: $10,000, $5,000 and $3,000.

name: Princeton Prize in Race Relations
who: U.S. high school students who led an activity in the last 12 months that advanced racial equity or understanding in their school or community. Grades are not considered. A sponsor who is not a relative completes part of the application.
notes: The prize site blocks automated reading. Directories list January 15, 2027; the 2025 application form said January 31. Winners also get a paid trip to the Symposium on Race at Princeton.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
sponsor: U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force with NSTA
who: High school students who have done original research in science, technology, engineering or math. You enter through your regional symposium; the top regional finalists go to the national symposium.
notes: National oral winners in each of eight categories get $12,000, $8,000 or $4,000, paid to their college over four years. Regional symposia run January to March 2027; regional paper deadlines come earlier. The 2027 national symposium is April 20-25 in Chantilly, Virginia.

name: Optimist International Essay Contest
who: Students under 19 on October 1 who have not finished high school. The 2026-27 topic is "Finding My Voice in a World Full of Noise." You enter through a local Optimist Club; club winners advance to the district contest.
notes: Each club sets its own deadline; club contests finish by early February. The $2,500 scholarship is awarded at the district level.

name: Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation Scholarships
amount: Varies; up to $10,000 a year for children of wounded Marines
who: Children of active duty, Reserve or honorably discharged U.S. Marines, or of Navy Corpsmen, Chaplains and Religious Program Specialists who served with Marines. Family adjusted gross income of $134,000 or less (2025 tax year), unless a parent was killed in service. Minimum 2.0 GPA.
notes: The undergraduate application is open every year from January 1 to March 1. Children of fallen Marines receive a guaranteed $30,000 over four years.

name: Gen and Kelly Tanabe Scholarship
who: Students in grades 9-12, college and graduate school who are legal U.S. residents. Winners are chosen mainly on a short personal statement.
notes: The sponsor's site does not show dates. Directories list two deadlines a year, July 31 and December 31.

name: JASNA Essay Contest
sponsor: Jane Austen Society of North America
who: High school and home-schooled students who write an essay on a set Jane Austen topic.
notes: The date shown is the 2026 deadline. The 2027 topic will be posted in November 2026 and entries open in February 2027. First place also gets a trip to JASNA's annual meeting (lodging and registration).

name: Pride Foundation Scholarships
amount: Varies (more than 60 funds; $1,000,000 to 121 students last year)
who: LGBTQ+ students who live in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon or Washington (or lived there for a year in the last five years) and will be in college, trade school or graduate school in 2027-28. U.S. citizenship is not required.
notes: One application covers all of the foundation's scholarship funds. Priority goes to students facing family rejection, financial need or housing instability.

name: Dr. Juan Andrade Jr. Scholarship for Young Hispanic Leaders
who: High school seniors and college students up to age 25 who will study full time at an accredited two- or four-year college in 2027-28 and show financial need. Meant for young Hispanic leaders; non-U.S. citizens may apply.
notes: One-time award. Letters of recommendation are also due December 30, 2026.

name: Elks Legacy Awards
who: High school seniors who are the child, grandchild, stepchild, step-grandchild or legal ward of an Elk who joined by April 1, 2024 and stays a dues-paying member through March 31, 2027.
notes: Deadline is 11:59 a.m. Pacific time. Only for Elks families; see Elks Most Valuable Student for the award open to everyone.
